speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I see you are a newborn presenting with respiratory distress; to better understand your condition, could you tell me if your mother had a difficult delivery or if you were born prematurely? REQUEST TEST: Maternal_history, Gestational_age. REQUEST TEST: Birth_weight.

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born after the 32nd gestational week. The baby was born via cesarean delivery. The mother had gestational diabetes but was otherwise healthy with no other pregnancy-related diseases.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Tachypnea, Subcostal and intercostal retractions, Nasal flaring, Cyanosis. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Transient Tachypnea of the Newborn (TTN). Based on the presence of tachypnea, retractions, nasal flaring, and cyanosis in a newborn, combined with the initial query about delivery history, these findings are highly suggestive of TTN, a condition often associated with delayed clearance of fetal lung fluid. Immediate chest imaging is recommended to confirm the diagnosis, but given your request for the most likely answer now, TTN is the primary consideration.
